PLANTING_PLAN.summary: Chosen in October 2026 for a short-season, frost-prone U-pick orchard at about 4,750 ft (the frost dates are on the site climate page). Disease-resistant apples that ripen early or in mid-season fill R4 to R6 and the grafted row R1; hardy tart and sweet cherries and a Seckel pear fill R8 to R10; and the shared stone-fruit rows R11 and R12 get two plums, one apricot, six peaches, and one Bing cherry in the spot that had been the Chinese (Mormon) apricot. Three of the peaches replace ones that died in their pots, and two more Intrepid trees replace the Mount Royal plums. R13 to R15 stay open for later.
PLANTING_PLAN.rootstock_advice: Ask nurseries for semi-dwarf trees (about 60 to 75 percent of standard; G.890, G.214 or M.7 for apples). The grid is 18 x 20 ft and the site is dry and windy, so dwarf stocks (M.27, M.9, B.9) would need permanent stakes and leave gaps.
PLANTING_PLAN.graft_advice: The 13 grafts in R1 go onto rootstocks you already own: 11 M-111 (vigorous, semi-standard), 2 EMLA 7 (semi-dwarf) and 1 of unknown type, so one rootstock is left as a spare. Order scionwood in winter from a nursery that sells it for spring 2027 (some sell out early), keep it cold and damp until grafting, and graft in early spring as the rootstock buds begin to swell. Use the two EMLA 7 rootstocks for Redfree, a vigorous scion (its third tree goes on an M-111), and put lower-vigor scions such as Pixie Crunch on the vigorous M-111. Grafted trees take longer to bear than bought trees. Check that a cultivar may be propagated at home before ordering scionwood.
PLANTING_PLAN.shipping_note: Confirm that each nursery ships the item to Idaho before ordering; some retailers exclude Idaho for some items. Cummins Nursery accepted the apple order below for Idaho and charged a phytosanitary certificate, but its checkout will not send peach, plum, cherry, nectarine, or apricot trees, scion, or rootstock there. Orange Pippin Trees USA and Willis Orchard Company each accepted a cherry order for Idaho on October 28. That acceptance is for those orders only.

items.caution: The flavor is unusual, like raspberry candy, and it is best fresh: about six weeks, though Cummins also lists one to three months. The tree is upright, so spread the branches. Cummins says somewhat resistant to fire blight, scab, and cedar-apple rust, not immune.

items.rootstock: All three are ordered on peach seedling, Field Ready, about 10 to 15 ft, a normal peach, not a staked dwarf. R11-C10 is Roots to Fruits order RTF12645. R11-C7 and R12-C7 are Roots to Fruits order WZTA0LZIJ, ships 5 to 6 ft or 5/8 in caliper
items.role: Best all-around peach for this site: bud-hardy, self-fertile, firmer than Reliance, ripe about two weeks after Redhaven
items.caution: NC State's patent for Intrepid (PP12357) records about a 40 percent crop at Sandhills in 1996, when the commercial varieties in those plots set nothing after six freezing nights in flower. It ripens about two weeks after Redhaven, earlier than Contender's 16 to 20 days in the University of Kentucky HO-6 table, so it has a better chance of finishing before an early September frost here. The fruit is firmer and larger than Reliance, with high bacterial spot resistance. It does not win every category: Contender is the better-documented flavor peach, Utah State lists Contender as frost tolerant, and the living Contender at R11-C8 was not flagged for bacterial canker. Reliance is hardier and earlier but soft. R11-C7 and R12-C7 replace the Mount Royal plums and are ordered on Roots to Fruits WZTA0LZIJ, charged $149, on seedling rather than the Lovell or Bailey that was the first ask. Peaches here carry bacterial canker (untreated positives): prune only in dry weather, use dormant copper, and buy clean certified stock.

items.caution: A second Contender, so you can compare it with the tree you already have. Utah State lists it as very cold hardy and tolerant of spring frost, but it ripens a few weeks after Redhaven, so it is a mid-season peach in a short season. Peaches here carry bacterial canker (untreated positives): prune only in dry weather, use dormant copper, and buy clean certified stock.
